chunks: "I'd group the rules by what the probe needs.
Pad: a bare copper pad, mask opened, about 1 mm in diameter or larger, with a finish that survives probing, and not covered by silkscreen.
Smaller works with finer probes but alignment gets tight. Spacing: pads on a grid with at least about 1. 27 mm centre-to-centre, and wider if the fixture vendor wants 2.
Keep them away from tall components, typically a millimetre or more from the part body, and from the board edge, so the fixture plate and the probe sit flat.
Side: put them all on one side, usually the bottom, because a two-sided fixture is more expensive and slower. Include two tooling holes at asymmetric positions.
Connection: connect each pad directly to its net with a short trace, ideally on the net itself so there's no stub.
On a fast net, make the pad the net's trace, in-line, or use a very short stub. Ground: put ground pads near signal pads and spread several around the board.
And label them on the silkscreen, away from the pad, and make sure no vias or components sit under the probe area. Then I'd check against the factory's DFT guideline."
